diagnostics.message: `:resource.google_project_iam_binding.authoritative` only references `google_project.project`, so it can be applied before the APIs in `var.services` are enabled. The members it binds often include service agents that are created only when their API is enabled (e.g. `<project_number>@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com`), and disabling services on destroy with surviving bindings can error. It should depend on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` (e.g. via depends_on, as already done for `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta`).

`:resource.google_project_iam_member.additive` grants roles to members supplied by the caller, which commonly include per-service service accounts (cloudservices, container-engine-robot, containerregistry, appspot, etc.) that only exist after `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` enables the corresponding APIs. Without that ordering the binding fails with "service account does not exist".

`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_admins` grants `roles/compute.osAdminLogin` on a new project but only depends on `google_project.project`, so it can run before `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` enables the Compute API. Granting service-specific roles / service-agent members before the API exists fails, so it should be ordered after service enablement.

`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_users` grants `roles/compute.osLogin` but is not ordered after `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`, so it may be applied before the Compute API is enabled; bindings referencing service roles/agents can fail in that window.

`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_compute_viewer` grants `roles/compute.viewer` without any ordering against `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`, so it can race service enablement on a freshly created project.

`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_iam_serviceaccountuser` grants `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` to OS Login admins/users but does not depend on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`; it should be applied after service enablement (and after the service agents those members reference exist).
